scope.description: 2026-09-04 WTypora 设计规格、当前分支全部一方源码、桌面文件能力、安全边界、测试、构建、macOS 打包及本机安装启动
included: package.json, package-lock.json, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, Tauri/Vite/TypeScript/ESLint configuration
excluded: node_modules and Cargo registry: third-party source
dist and src-tauri/target internals: generated build output; final bundles were separately verified
real-world penetration testing: outside static/local safety-audit boundary

evidence: Design sections 2.1-2.5 map to src/app, src/document, src/editor, src/export and src-tauri/src/commands; README.md:36-49 records the delivered feature set.
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-04-wtypora-implementation.md provides the implementation-to-verification sequence.
VisualEditor and SourceEditor share EditorAdapter/Markdown, while documentStore owns the persisted baseline and save state.
68 frontend assertions and 16 Rust integration tests exercise the specified file, editor, conflict, image, export and watcher behavior.
git diff review covers 38 changed first-party files and preserves existing editors, export, preference and workspace modules.
Final independent review reported no remaining Critical or Important issue and Ready to merge: Yes.
Markdown remains the sole disk interchange format; standard and empty YAML Front Matter are preserved by src/document/frontMatter.ts.
NativeBridge types retain browser-test and Tauri implementations; Node 26/npm 11/Rust 1.88 requirements match locked dependencies.
src/document/documentStore.ts and src/app/useAppCommands.ts enforce session IDs, save queues, disk digests and explicit state transitions.
Editor contract tests validate source/visual content, cursor, find/replace, outline and Front Matter behavior.
Tests cover empty Front Matter, unsupported images, hidden/build directories, symlink escapes, duplicate names and missing authorization.
Mermaid, math, footnote and local-image export paths have success and error/boundary assertions.
Open requests and watcher callbacks are request/session guarded; stale success and stale rejection do not alter the active session.
File watch setup releases its event listener when native watch creation fails; cleanup stops both listener and native watch.
Errors remain typed across Rust/TypeScript, save failures keep memory content dirty, and command errors are visible/dismissible.
Review fixes address root races using optimistic digests and atomic destination reservation rather than timing workarounds.
The single-user local app has no account or remote object boundary; Rust enforces OS-dialog file grants and distinguishes individual-file from directory authorization.
Asset protocol authorization is dynamically limited to the active document's exact assets directory.
Canonical path checks reject traversal and symlink escape; image writes restrict extensions and use create_new collision-safe files.
HTML sanitization removes scriptable elements/attributes/URLs; Mermaid uses strict mode and print images use authorized asset URLs.
Source/config review found no embedded password, token or private document fixture; the app is local-only and does not upload content.
Displayed errors include actionable paths but no credential-bearing request or remote response data.
npm audit --omit=dev completed with 0 vulnerabilities.
package and Cargo locks are committed inputs; CSP and an empty static asset scope constrain WebView capabilities.
No network API, authentication session, CSRF surface or multi-user replay boundary exists in the specified product scope.
Local abuse resistance is risk-matched through explicit file grants, bounded Mermaid input settings and supported-type filtering.
Rust saves write, sync and atomically rename a unique temporary file; failure cleanup preserves the original destination.
Existing file permissions are preserved and verified by filesystem integration tests.
Document defaults, nullable path/digest values, UTF-8 content and empty/non-empty YAML Front Matter are explicitly handled and tested.
No database schema or migration is introduced; persisted Markdown and preference formats remain compatible.
Frontend saves are serialized and use expected-digest compare-and-swap semantics before replacement.
Eight-thread same-name image integration test proves atomic create_new reservation prevents overwrite under concurrency.
Recovery drafts retain unnamed or failed-write content; discard removes only the matching recovery ID.
External changes and failed optimistic writes become explicit conflicts without overwriting either local memory or disk silently.
Workspace scanning prunes hidden, dependency and build directories and ignores symlinks; editor statistics and outline operations are linear in document size.
Save debounce and serialized writes avoid repeated overlapping disk I/O.
Release package measured 15 MB for WTypora.app and 8.4 MB for the DMG; build completed and installed app launched successfully in the bounded verification.
No pre-existing formal latency/size baseline exists; production build warns that the main JavaScript entry is 2,145.91 kB (CQ-001).
Editor disposal, menu listeners, file-watch listeners and native watch IDs have explicit cleanup guards.
Mermaid text/edge limits, 800 ms autosave debounce and collision attempts keep key resources bounded.
The runtime has no required cloud service; native and rendering failures surface locally while preserving Markdown source.
Mermaid/KaTeX failure paths degrade to visible error/source content instead of losing the rest of the document.
Document, editor, native, workspace and export responsibilities follow design section 4.2 and the existing directory architecture.
File operations remain behind NativeBridge and Rust commands rather than leaking into editor components.
Shared frontMatter and imageUrl helpers remove duplicated parsing/path rules; save coordination uses one command hook and one queue.
No new framework or parallel persistence mechanism was introduced.
TypeScript and Rust control flow use typed results, descriptive session/digest names and explicit early returns for stale work.
ESLint and Clippy with warnings denied both complete successfully.
NativeBridge has a replaceable in-memory implementation and EditorAdapter allows both editors to share contract tests.
Export image resolution is injected, making browser export and WebView printing independently testable.
npm run lint -- --max-warnings 0 and cargo clippy -- -D warnings report no warning, dead-code or debug-build blocker.
git diff --check reports no whitespace error.
npm test -- --run: 14 files and 68 tests passed, exit 0.
cargo test --locked: 15 filesystem and 1 watcher tests passed, exit 0.
New tests directly constrain save ordering, async-open freshness, error UI, visual cursor/find/outline, printing, asset URLs and Front Matter.
Rust tests directly constrain digest conflicts, file-vs-directory grants, symlink escapes and concurrent image naming.
Concurrency, stale async work, partial failure, authorization, XSS sanitation, collision and recovery paths all have targeted assertions.
Final review independently traced high-value data flows after the tests passed.
Regression evidence combines frontend component/unit tests, Rust integration tests, static analysis, production packaging, signature checks and a live launch.
Assertions verify content/state/hash/authorization outcomes rather than relying on test counts alone.

Installed /Applications/WTypora.app version 0.1.0 launched as PID 7412 and matched release binary/icon SHA-256 values.
Typed native errors preserve code/message/path; save and command failures remain visible and dismissible in the UI.
No secrets or document contents are emitted by the verified build/install commands.
README.md:5-34 records toolchain, install, development and verification commands.

findings.evidence: Vite production build succeeds but reports a 2,145.91 kB main JavaScript entry above the 500 kB advisory threshold.
findings.impact: Cold start and parse cost may grow for very resource-constrained machines; correctness and local data integrity are unaffected.
verification: npm run build (exit 0; inspect Vite size report)
findings.recommendation: Future performance work should lazy-load heavy editor/diagram modules and establish a startup/size baseline.

findings.evidence: The local package is ad-hoc signed and passes deep strict verification, but it is not Apple Developer ID signed or notarized.
findings.impact: The requested local installation works; public distribution to other Macs would require a release identity and notarization credentials.
findings.recommendation: Before public distribution, configure Developer ID Application signing and Apple notarization.
